Writing the cross-process probe now.

# Review of 670df28f7bf7: session pause holds model requests at the dispatch boundary

I measured one defect, and it should be fixed before merge. I ran it with two real processes.

## 1. Move the `/pause` hold ahead of the in-flight slot: a paused process holds the cross-process slot for the whole pause (P1)

**File:** `packages/ai/src/stream.ts:690-701`, in `withProviderInFlightLimit`.

**Mechanism:**
- The patch acquires the provider in-flight lease first (`acquireProviderInFlightSlot`) and only then runs `await holdBeforeDispatch(hold, options?.signal)`. The comment says "Last, so the slot wait above cannot outlast it".
- That lease is not in-process state. It is a directory under the shared in-flight root, and a heartbeat refreshes it every `PROVIDER_INFLIGHT_HEARTBEAT_MS` (5s).
- So a request parked on `/pause` keeps the lease alive the whole time. The stale-lease reaper (`PROVIDER_INFLIGHT_LEASE_STALE_MS`, 30s) never reclaims it.
- Every other omp process using that provider with a `maxInFlightRequests` cap is blocked until a human resumes the paused one. `agentPauseGate` is per process, so those other sessions were never paused.
- Before the patch this could not happen:
  - The agent loop polled the gate before `streamFn`, so before any slot was taken.
  - Side requests (compaction, titles, memory, judge, and so on) had no hold at all.
- The patch also routes every agent-loop request and every `#sideStreamFn` request through this hold: `agent-loop.ts:2179`, `agent-session.ts:2256`, `session-maintenance.ts:3721/5637`. A side request issued while paused is enough to trigger it.

**Trigger:** I used two processes with the same in-flight root and limit 1 on provider `tests`, using the real `streamSimple` with the mock API and the real `agentPauseGate`:
- **Holder:** calls `agentPauseGate.pause()`, then `streamSimple(model, ctx, { maxInFlightRequests: { tests: 1 }, beforeDispatch: agentPauseGate.dispatchHold() })`. It stays paused for `HOLD_MS`.
- **Contender:** a separate process that is never paused. It sends the same `streamSimple` with `maxInFlightRequests: { tests: 1 }`.

The probe is `scratch/.../shared/inflight-proc.ts`. Run it from `packages/ai`:

```
R=$(mktemp -d); HOLD_MS=40000 bun inflight-proc.ts holder $R & sleep 1.5; bun inflight-proc.ts contender $R; wait
```

**Measured:** the unpaused contender waited 38.6s, which is past the 30s stale window. It was sent only when the other process resumed:

```
[holder +9ms] holder request issued while paused; staying paused
[contender +1ms] contender (not paused) issuing request
[holder +40013ms] holder resuming
[holder +40018ms] provider dispatched
[holder +40027ms] holder done
[contender +38644ms] provider dispatched
[contender +38647ms] contender result stopReason=stop
```

A 3s hold gave the same result: the contender was dispatched at +1823ms, as soon as the holder resumed. While the holder was paused, its lease directory was present under the shared root.

**Fix direction:**
- Run the hold before `acquireProviderInFlightSlot`, and re-check the gate after acquiring.
- Or release the lease while parked and acquire it again after the hold.

The gap the author was worried about ("slot wait outlasts the hold") is still covered by the transport-level hold in `transportFetch`. That hold runs after the slot anyway.

## Not measured (hypothesis)

**Codex websocket reuse after a long pause.** In `openai-codex-responses.ts:4621-4627`, the `isHealthyForReuse()` check returns the reused socket before any hold. The send-path hold at line 4160 then parks on that socket for the length of the pause. After it, only `readyState === OPEN` is checked again (lines 4165-4166). The code's own comment cites issue #1450: a socket the server evicted can still read OPEN. If so, a long `/pause` would make the resumed request go into a half-open socket and wait out the first-event timeout.

To settle it: run the existing `codex-pause-dispatch.test.ts` harness with a server that stops replying on an idle socket while it reports OPEN. Pause past the reuse health window, resume, and time how long the request takes to fail or succeed.

**Verdict:** not safe to merge as is. Pausing one process stalls other, unpaused omp processes on any provider that has an in-flight cap, for as long as the pause lasts.
